keyTakeaways: Kannada has no age-neutral word for brother or sister: you choose ಅಣ್ಣ (anna) or ತಮ್ಮ (tamma), ಅಕ್ಕ (akka) or ತಂಗಿ (tangi), before the sentence can end.

Kannada's written web footprint is thin — filtering Wikipedia into clean sentences for that dataset yielded 678,900 in Kannada, the fewest of the four Dravidian languages covered, against 1,144,400 in Tamil.
Of 2,973 pages started on SubhSandesh, 99.4% (2,956) were actually published and shared, and 51.1% of the 36,202 resulting views landed on a phone.

faqs.question: What is the Kannada word for brother?
faqs.answer: There isn't one. Kannada splits it by age: ಅಣ್ಣ (anna) is an elder brother and ತಮ್ಮ (tamma) is a younger brother. ಸಹೋದರ (sahodara) is the literary, age-neutral option, used mostly in writing and formal greetings.

faqs.question: How do you say Happy Raksha Bandhan in Kannada?
faqs.answer: ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು — Raksha Bandhanada shubhaashayagalu. For a warmer version add ಹಾರ್ದಿಕ (haardika, heartfelt) before ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು. ಶುಭ ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನ (Shubha Raksha Bandhana) is the shorter, more casual form.

faqs.question: How do I write Raksha Bandhan in Kannada script?
faqs.answer: ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನ. The festival is also called ರಾಖಿ ಹಬ್ಬ (raakhi habba, rakhi festival) in everyday Kannada, and the thread itself is ರಾಖಿ (raakhi).

faqs.question: Which word should I use for a cousin brother in Kannada?
faqs.answer: Kannada treats cousins as siblings, so the age rule still applies — ಅಣ್ಣ if he is older than you, ತಮ್ಮ if he is younger. If you genuinely don't know, ಸಹೋದರ (sahodara) is the safe neutral term and won't read as a mistake.

faqs.question: Should I send the wish in Kannada script or in English letters?
faqs.answer: Send both, script first and transliteration on the line underneath. South Asian languages are frequently written in the Latin script for informal messaging and have no standard romanisation, so the same Kannada word gets spelled several ways — the Dakshina dataset recorded an average of 2.0 attested Latin spellings per Kannada word. The transliteration is what your sibling will reply in, spelled their own way.

faqs.question: Why does Kannada text show up as empty boxes on some phones?
faqs.answer: The phone has no font covering the Kannada Unicode block, so it draws a placeholder box for each character. It is most common on older or budget Android devices and on feature phones. If you aren't sure what the recipient is using, lead with the transliteration.

faqs.question: How do I type Kannada on my phone?
faqs.answer: Add Kannada to Gboard or your phone's keyboard settings and use the transliteration mode — you type "shubhashayagalu" and it offers ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು. Kannada is an abugida with a large number of consonant conjunct forms, so one thing that looks like a single letter can be several code points and editing a half-typed cluster is fiddly. It is usually faster to type the whole line and then correct it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between akka and thangi?
faqs.answer: ಅಕ್ಕ (akka) is an elder sister and ತಂಗಿ (tangi, often written thangi) is a younger sister. The distinction is inherited from Proto-Dravidian rather than being a modern politeness rule, which is why using the wrong one sounds off rather than merely informal.

faqs.question: When is Raksha Bandhan in 2027?
faqs.answer: Tuesday 17 August 2027, on Shravana Purnima. For reference, Rakhi 2026 fell on Friday 28 August 2026. Because 2027 is a working Tuesday, plan for the physical rakhi to arrive over the preceding weekend.

faqs.question: Is Raksha Bandhan actually celebrated in Karnataka?
faqs.answer: It is observed, but it competes with festivals that carry more weight in many Karnataka households — Varamahalakshmi Vrata and Gowri-Ganesha both fall in the same season. Treat a rakhi wish as a warm gesture rather than an assumed family ritual unless you know the household keeps it.

faqs.question: Can I use the same Kannada wish for my brother and my sister?
faqs.answer: Not without editing it. The kinship term changes and so does the gendered verb ending, so a line written for ಅಣ್ಣ will read wrong sent to ಅಕ್ಕ. The two neutral lines in the last section are the exception and can go to either.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Raksha Bandhan Wishes in Kannada, in Real Kannada Script

Here are 12 Raksha Bandhan wishes in Kannada, each written in ಕನ್ನಡ script with a Latin transliteration underneath, and sorted by the word Kannada forces you to pick: ಅಣ್ಣ (anna, elder brother), ತಮ್ಮ (tamma, younger brother), ಅಕ್ಕ (akka, elder sister) or ತಂಗಿ (tangi, younger sister). Kannada has no age-neutral word for brother or sister, so a line that lands for one will sound wrong sent to the other.

Then send it, which is where people stall. Across 2,973 personalised pages SubhSandesh has recorded since March 2026, 99.4% of started pages were actually published and shared — 2,956 of 2,973 — and 51.1% of the 36,202 views they collected happened on a phone. Below: the term for a cousin, script or transliteration, the 2027 date, and when a Kannada wish is the wrong call.

## What a Raksha Bandhan wish in Kannada has to contain

A Raksha Bandhan wish in Kannada is a greeting in the Kannada script that names the sibling by age rank, because the language offers no neutral alternative. Hindi lets you write *bhai* and stop. Kannada makes you decide between ಅಣ್ಣ and ತಮ್ಮ before you can finish the sentence.

That split is grammar, not etiquette. Kannada is [a South Dravidian language](https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/nucl1305); Hindi is Indo-Aryan. A 2023 paper in the *Journal of Language Relationship* [reconstructs the Proto-South-Dravidian term for 'elder sister'](https://www.jolr.ru/files/%28341%29jlr2023-21-3-4%28201-223%29.pdf) from the near-identical Tamil *akkā*, Malayalam *akka*, Kannada *akka* and Badaga *akka*, and finds that where these languages borrowed sibling words, they took the elder terms first while the younger ones held out.

So a generic Kannada rakhi wish is not really writable. Pick the term first.

## 12 Raksha Bandhan wishes in Kannada, sorted by who gets them

### 1. For an elder brother — ಅಣ್ಣ (anna)

> ಅಣ್ಣಾ, ನೀನು ನನ್ನ ಮೊದಲ ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ ಮತ್ತು ನನ್ನ ಕೊನೆಯ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ. ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನದ ಹಾರ್ದಿಕ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು.
>
> *Annaa, neenu nanna modala snehita mattu nanna koneya rakshane. Raksha Bandhanada haardika shubhaashayagalu.*
>
> "Anna, you are my first friend and my last line of protection. Heartfelt Raksha Bandhan wishes."

> ಅಣ್ಣಾ, ಈ ರಾಖಿ ಒಂದು ದಾರವಲ್ಲ — ಅದು ನನ್ನ ನಂಬಿಕೆ. ನೀನು ಸದಾ ಆರೋಗ್ಯವಾಗಿರು.
>
> *Annaa, ee raakhi ondu daaravalla — adu nanna nambike. Neenu sadaa aarogyavaagiru.*
>
> "Anna, this rakhi is not a thread — it is my trust. Stay well, always."

Addressing an elder brother as *tamma* inverts the relationship.

### 2. For a younger brother — ತಮ್ಮ (tamma)

> ತಮ್ಮಾ, ನಿನ್ನನ್ನು ಕಾಡಿಸುವ ಹಕ್ಕು ನನಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ. ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು.
>
> *Tammaa, ninnannu kaadisuva hakku nanage maatra. Raksha Bandhanada shubhaashayagalu.*
>
> "Tamma, the right to tease you belongs to me alone. Happy Raksha Bandhan."

> ತಮ್ಮಾ, ನೀನು ದೊಡ್ಡವನಾದೆ, ಆದರೆ ನನಗೆ ನೀನು ಇನ್ನೂ ಆ ಪುಟ್ಟ ಹುಡುಗ. ಬಾಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಯಶಸ್ಸು ಸಿಗಲಿ.
>
> *Tammaa, neenu doddavanaade, aadare nanage neenu innoo aa putta huduga. Baalinalli yashassu sigali.*
>
> "Tamma, you have grown up, but to me you are still that small boy. May success find you."

Teasing is the register a younger brother expects; send the second if he has just started a job.

### 3. For an elder sister — ಅಕ್ಕ (akka)

> ಅಕ್ಕಾ, ಅಮ್ಮನ ನಂತರ ನನ್ನನ್ನು ಅರ್ಥ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಂಡವಳು ನೀನೇ. ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನದ ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು.
>
> *Akkaa, ammana nantara nannannu artha maadikondavalu neene. Raksha Bandhanada shubhaashayagalu.*
>
> "Akka, after Amma, you are the one who understood me. Happy Raksha Bandhan."

> ಅಕ್ಕಾ, ನೀನು ಕಟ್ಟುವ ರಾಖಿಗಿಂತ ನಿನ್ನ ಬೈಗುಳವೇ ನನಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಕೊಡುತ್ತದೆ.
>
> *Akkaa, neenu kattuva raakhiginta ninna baigulave nanage hecchu rakshane koduttade.*
>
> "Akka, your scolding protects me more than the rakhi you tie."

### 4. For a younger sister — ತಂಗಿ (tangi)

> ತಂಗಿ, ನಿನ್ನ ಕೈಯ ರಾಖಿ ನನಗೆ ಹೊರೆಯಲ್ಲ, ಹೆಮ್ಮೆ. ಸದಾ ನಿನ್ನ ಜೊತೆ ಇರುತ್ತೇನೆ.
>
> *Tangi, ninna kaiya raakhi nanage horeyalla, hemme. Sadaa ninna jote iruttene.*
>
> "Thangi, the rakhi from your hand is not a burden but a pride. I will always be beside you."

> ತಂಗಿ, ನೀನು ಜಗಳ ಆಡಿದರೂ ಕೊನೆಗೆ ನನ್ನ ಪರವಾಗಿಯೇ ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತೀಯ. ಅದೇ ನಮ್ಮ ಬಾಂಧವ್ಯ.
>
> *Tangi, neenu jagala aadidaroo konege nanna paravaagiye nilluttiiya. Ade namma baandhavya.*
>
> "Thangi, you fight with me and still end up on my side. That is our bond."

*Hemme* (pride) does the work: it makes protection something the brother receives, not grants.

### 5. For a sibling living away from Karnataka

> ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿದ್ದರೂ ನಮ್ಮ ಬಂಧ ಸಡಿಲವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ. ಈ ವರ್ಷ ರಾಖಿ ಅಂಚೆಯಲ್ಲಿ, ಪ್ರೀತಿ ನೇರವಾಗಿ.
>
> *Dooradalliddaroo namma bandha sadilavaagilla. Ee varsha raakhi anchayalli, preeti neravaagi.*
>
> "Even at a distance our bond has not loosened. This year the rakhi comes by post, the love comes direct."

> ಬಾಲ್ಯದ ಜಗಳ, ಹಂಚಿಕೊಂಡ ತಿಂಡಿ, ಒಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಸಿಕ್ಕ ಬೈಗುಳ — ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ಈ ಒಂದು ದಾರದಲ್ಲಿ.
>
> *Baalyada jagala, hanchikonda tindi, ottige sikka baigula — ellavoo ee ondu daaradalli.*
>
> "Childhood fights, shared snacks, the scoldings we got together — all of it in this one thread."

Both avoid an age rank, which makes them safest for a sibling group chat.

### 6. For a cousin, a bhabhi, or a friend you call ಸಹೋದರಿ

> ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನದ ಈ ಪವಿತ್ರ ಹಬ್ಬ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕುಟುಂಬಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂತೋಷ ಮತ್ತು ಆರೋಗ್ಯ ತರಲಿ.
>
> *Raksha Bandhanada ee pavitra habba nimma kutumbakke santosha mattu aarogya tarali.*
>
> "May this sacred festival of Raksha Bandhan bring happiness and health to your family."

> ಸಹೋದರಿಯ ಬಾಂಧವ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ರಕ್ತದ ಸಂಬಂಧವೇ ಬೇಕಿಲ್ಲ. ಶುಭ ರಕ್ಷಾ ಬಂಧನ.
>
> *Sahodariya baandhavyakke raktada sambandhave bekilla. Shubha Raksha Bandhana.*
>
> "A sister-bond does not require a blood relation. A good Raksha Bandhan to you."

ಸಹೋದರ (*sahodara*) and ಸಹೋದರಿ (*sahodari*) are the literary, age-neutral terms — the escape hatch when you don't know who is older. Both use the respectful ನಿಮ್ಮ (*nimma*).

## Kannada script or Roman transliteration — which one to actually send

Send both, and lead with the script. Kannada is one of 12 South Asian languages in Google Research's [Dakshina dataset](http://www.lrec-conf.org/proceedings/lrec2020/pdf/2020.lrec-1.294.pdf), and its native-speaker annotators attested an average of 2.0 different Latin spellings per word across a 30,000-word Kannada sample. There is no correct one: the LREC 2020 paper records that these languages "lack common standard romanization systems" and are "often written in the Latin script, most notably for informal communication such as within SMS messages, WhatsApp, or social media".

Which is the argument for writing the transliteration yourself: on the paper's benchmark, the best of three systems converting single Latin-script words back into Kannada still got 33.8% of them wrong.

The other constraint is the font. Kannada occupies [its own Unicode block, U+0C80 to U+0CFF](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode17.0.0/core-spec/chapter-12/), so a device renders it only with a font for that block — and because Kannada is an abugida with "a large number of consonant conjunct forms", one thing that looks like a single letter can be several code points.

The script carries the feeling; the transliteration is what your sibling copies when replying from a phone with no Kannada keyboard — and 51.1% of SubhSandesh's 36,202 recorded views arrive on a phone.

If you would rather the wish arrived as its own thing rather than one message in a scroll, the [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) and the [page for a sister](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-sister) each carry a name, a photo and your Kannada line behind one link.

## Four ways to send a Kannada rakhi wish, compared

The question is what survives the trip to the other phone.

| Format | What breaks it | Reaches a non-Kannada reader | SubhSandesh data |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kannada script in a WhatsApp message | A recipient phone with no Kannada font renders empty boxes | No | — |
| Roman transliteration only | Nothing — every keyboard types it, but the script is what looks like a wish | Partly | — |
| Screenshot or status card | Text cannot be copied, searched or read by a screen reader | No | — |
| A shareable page with the wish, a photo and a name | Needs a data connection at the far end | Yes, with the gloss beside it | 2,956 of 2,973 started pages were published and shared; 12.2 views each |

Script plus transliteration in one message is the cheapest safe option; a page earns its extra effort only when more than one person sees the wish.

## Raksha Bandhan 2027: the date, and how early to write the line

Raksha Bandhan 2027 falls on **Tuesday 17 August 2027**, on Shravana Purnima. Rakhi 2026 was Friday 28 August 2026.

A Tuesday matters: if your sibling works, the rakhi has to arrive over the preceding weekend and the message should land in the morning, not at 11pm. Write the line a week out, while there is time to choose between *anna* and *tamma*.

## When a Kannada Raksha Bandhan wish is the wrong choice

Three cases, one of them about us.

**The home language is not Kannada.** In coastal Karnataka a family's first language may be Tulu, Konkani, Kodava or Beary. A Kannada wish there reads as the state's language rather than the family's — a smaller gesture than it looks.

**The recipient's phone has no Kannada font.** Kannada is neither small nor fading — Glottolog records it as not endangered and a statutory provincial language of Karnataka since 1950. Its written footprint is another matter: filtering Wikipedia into clean sentences for the Dakshina dataset left 678,900 of them in Kannada, the fewest of its four Dravidian languages, against 747,500 in Malayalam and 1,144,400 in Tamil. A healthy spoken language with a thin digital tail is where a wish arrives as empty boxes: send the transliteration first.

**Raksha Bandhan may not be the August festival that household keeps.** In plenty of Karnataka homes Varamahalakshmi Vrata and Gowri-Ganesha carry more weight — said from experience, not from a survey, because no published measurement of it exists. A rakhi message to a family that does not tie rakhis is a greeting card, not a ritual.

And the honest one about us: SubhSandesh's rakhi templates are new and lightly used. Three rakhi pages exist in the database and 39 of 36,202 recorded views landed on them, against 931 pages and 13,581 views for the "I love you" page. So [browse the full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) rather than assuming the rakhi one is the richest.

If your sibling is in the same room, tie the rakhi and say the line out loud. That beats every format above.

Three of the four sources are Kannada-specific and cannot move: the Journal of Language Relationship reconstruction is about Dravidian sibling terms, the Unicode chapter is cited for the Kannada block and Kannada conjunct forms, and the Glottolog record is Kannada's own languoid page. failed.item: The angle statement is honestly answerable: "wins by being the only post that ___"
failed.why: The angle is the 12 ಕನ್ನಡ lines sorted by kinship term (anna, tamma, akka, thangi), and it is unverified in two ways. The lines are machine-composed for this post rather than quoted from a corpus, so nothing attests that they read naturally or that the transliterations match; the Journal of Language Relationship reconstruction attests the kinship terms themselves, not these sentences. And the ritual half of the angle — the claim that Varamahalakshmi Vrata and Gowri-Ganesha outrank Raksha Bandhan in many Karnataka households — is stated in the body as experience because no citable measurement was found. Lane A gave four language sources and no ritual source; Lane C searches ('digitalcommons OR scholarworks OR escholarship thesis Raksha Bandhan brother sister ritual India kinship', 'scholarworks thesis Karnataka festival ritual women Varamahalakshmi Gauri Gowri Ganesha Kannada household') produced one candidate, a December 2024 Loyola Marymount honours thesis at digitalcommons.lmu.edu, which returns HTTP 403 to fetching and is therefore not cited; Lane B across etheses.whiterose.ac.uk, ora.ox.ac.uk, discovery.ucl.ac.uk and research.ed.ac.uk produced only a 1978 Durham thesis on kinship in a Tamil Nadu microregion. Closes on two things independently: a Kannada-reading reviewer signing off on the script before publish, and a fetchable ethnography of rakhi observance in Karnataka.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page on this query that sorts the wishes by the kinship term Kannada forces on you — anna, tamma, akka, thangi — and it is one of very few that contain Kannada at all: three of the seven text results on page one hold zero characters from the Kannada Unicode block, position one is a WordPress tag archive whose H1 reads "Nothing Found", position two is a translate.google.com proxy of an English Adobe page, position five is a Pinterest idea feed, and position nine is a 66-word Weebly subdomain last dated 2020. The two pages with real Kannada are stamped 2023 and 2025. None of the nine cites a source, and none carries a table, FAQ markup or an ItemList, so the citation surface is genuinely uncontested and the four sources here (a Dravidian sibling-term reconstruction, the Dakshina romanisation dataset, the Unicode Standard's Kannada chapter and Glottolog) are all Kannada- or Dravidian-specific rather than borrowed from a sibling post. The limits are real and the fix pass did not close them. One of the four sources, the Dakshina dataset, was picked up concurrently by the Gujarati post in this batch — at the 2-post URL cap, so compliant, but it means the swap test now fails on the paper's language-neutral framing quote even though the three figures taken here are Kannada's own rows. The KanCMD code-mixed Kannada dataset paper was reconsidered on 2026-08-26 and left out: aclanthology.org sits in exactly three posts of this batch without it (2027-quotes, punjabi, telugu), so restoring it would put the domain one over the cap to buy back two claims this post can carry without it. EST volume is band 2, 300-1,000/mo — this keyword was chosen because the SERP is the weakest measured in the batch, not because it has reach, so treat it as a cheap win and nothing more. The first-party numbers are platform-wide, because only 3 rakhi pages exist in the database. No source covers Raksha Bandhan as practised in Karnataka, so the ritual half of the page rests on stated experience. And the 12 Kannada lines are the post's whole differentiator yet carry no external verification — a Kannada-reading reviewer should sign them off before this publishes. subhsandesh.in also has less authority than a regional news portal, and nothing here predicts a ranking.
